sources.text: Main text backbone. Large matrices use a BF16 reference except source FP32 operations and the explicitly stored FP8 Engram table with E8M0 scales. Checkpoint FP8/FP4 MoE and projection kernels, vision, DSpark, sampling need separate configurations.

BF16 attention caches represent active batch lanes in the reference fake-quant path. Physical cache grows by completed groups and preserves all provisioned local windows. The Engram token history reserves its configured context length; its precomputed token map uses the released embedding vocabulary as an upper bound.

CSA2 runs full index dot products before applying the candidate mask, as in the reference implementation. Sparse attention, hash, nonlinear and selection work use explicit analytical operation/traffic proxies. Pair counts use the published candidate dimensions and assume enough candidate entries for final Top-K; logical query chunks extend the reference initial prefill and single-token decode.

Local equations bind allocated request, head and expert extents. Lookup and sparse expert reads use explicit traffic equations. Link rates and analytical work proxies describe the configured estimate.

Each rank holds whole attention heads and matching output groups. Indexer query heads contribute FP32 partial scores, reduced before candidate selection or masking. Window, compressed latent, index K and compressor state are replicated, with one backing per shared cache on each rank. The row-parallel output partial uses an FP32 AllReduce before resuming the BF16 residual path.

Each EP rank owns a contiguous, equal count of routed experts. Each token keeps its global Top-K, with per-rank route budgets balanced by quotient and remainder. Allocated slots use ceil(K/EP). Useful work and sparse gathers use valid slots. The shared expert is replicated and added after reducing FP32 routed partials.

The combined V4.1 preset also shards the Engram weight and scale tables by rows, reserving ceil(rows/ranks) rows per rank. The lookup charges one read per requested hash on each rank, including the masked dummy row, and reduces the BF16 values before the replicated projection.
